sentences.text: The petitioners filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- from the respondents due to death of Sri. Hari Prasath, in the road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts of petitioners case is that, on 26-06-2023 at about 3.30 pm, the deceased was travelling as a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04/JH-1312 and proceeding on Jayanthi Nagara Main Road, Near D'Mart Ready Shop, Bangalore City, at that time, the rider of the said motorcycle drove the same in a very rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life and dashed to the bicycle and caused the accident.
As a result of forced impact, the deceased and rider were fell down, sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Sunrise Hospital, wherein first aid was given and further shifted to Nimhans Hospital, Bangalore for higher medication, inspite of better treatment he was died in the hospital.

After conducting the postmortem, the petitioners were shifted the dead body to their native place and performed the funeral, obsequies and last rites ceremony of the deceased, for which they spent more than Rs.2,00,000/-.
4.
At the time of accident, the deceased was aged about 19 years and enjoying good health.
He was working as an employee at Private Company and earning Rs.30,000/-p.m.

he was contributing his entire earnings to maintain the family and due to sudden death of the deceased the petitioners lost love and affection of the deceased and they are undergoing great mental shock and agony and also facing great financial difficulties.
The deceased is the only son of his parents.

sentences.text: This accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04/JH-1312.

Hence, the K.R. Puram Traffic Police have registered a case against rider of the said Motorcycle in Cr.No.189/2023 U/Sec.279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.
6.

The respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the offending Motorcycle, the policy was in force as on the date of accident and they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
7. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
The respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court and hence, she placed as Ex-parte.
8. Respondent No.1 in his written statement contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and it is liable to be dismissed in limine.

It is further contended that, it has issued the Act policy or liability only policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04/JH-1312 from 21-06-2023 till 20-06-2024.
It is further submitted that, there is no separate premium collected to cover the risk of pillion rider of the insured vehicle, as such the claim petition is liable to be dismissed.
It is further contended that,
respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy by handing over the vehicle to a minor to ride the said vehicle.
As per charge sheet in Cr.No.189/2023 the rider of the insured vehicle by name Sathyam Sharma was a minor and not holding the valid and effective D.L. at the time of accident.
The respondent No.1 under the contract of insurance is not obligated to indemnify the insured respondent No.2 and petition as against the respondent No.1 be rejected.

Further denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased and expenses incurred towards funeral ceremony of the deceased and contended that, claim of the petitioners is excessive, exorbitant & exaggerated.

Hence,
prayed to dismiss the petition with costs.

9. Based on the above pleadings, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that on 26-06- 2023 at about 3.30 pm, deceased Hari Prasath was proceeding as a pillion rider in a Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04/JH-1312 on Jayanthi Nagara Main Road, near D Mart Shop, Bangalore,
wherein the rider of the said motorcycle drove it, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering human life, without following any traffic rules and dashed against the Bicycle and caused the accident, due to forced impact deceased succumbed to the accidental injuries in the hospital?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so how much?

From whom?
3) Whether order or award?

sentences.text: In order to prove the case, petitioner No.1 got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 15 documents marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.

The respondent No.1 got examined its Claim Service Manager as RW.1 and got marked 02 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2.
11.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on hand.

12. For the following reasons, this Tribunal answer the above Issues as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS 13. Issue No.1:-
The petitioners filed this claim petition against respondents for claiming compensation due to death of their son by name Sri. Hari Prasath in a road traffic accident that occurred on 26-06-2023.

14. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 got examined himself as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination and he had reiterated the entire contention of petition and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of F.I.R, Ex.P.2 is the copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the copy of Sketch, Ex.P.5 is the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the copy of inquest report, Ex.P.7 is the copy of PM report, Ex.P.8 is the copy of charge sheet, Ex.P.9 is the copy of notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act, Ex.P.10 is the copy of reply to the notice, Ex.P.11 to 13 are the copies of Aadhar Cards, Ex.P.14 and 15 are the copies of certificates.
In cross examination, he has admitted that, the rider of the motorcycle was the minor.
Further he has stated that he gave the statement to the police.
15. To disprove the case, respondent No.1 has examined its Claim Service Manager as RW.1 and got marked 02 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2.
Ex.R.1 is the authorization letter, Ex.R.2 is the copy of insurance policy.
In chief examination he has stated that, the 1st respondent has issued a policy to the motorcycle.

The rider of the motorcycle was juvenile and not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and respondent No.2 has willfully allowed the minor to ride the motorcycle and thereby contravened the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, contended that, the respondent No.1 is not liable to indemnify respondent No.2.
In the cross-examination nothing worthy has been elicited.

16. As per Ex.P.4-sketch and Ex.P.8-charge sheet, it appears that, on the date of accident, the rider of offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04/JH-1312 along with the pillion rider both without wearing the helmets, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangerous to human life, came from Raghavendra Circle towards Jayanthinagar and dashed to one bicycle at the middle of the road and caused the accident.
As a result of which the deceased Hari Prasath was sustained grievous injuries and the deceased died in the hospital.

Hence, the K.R. Puram Traffic Police have filed charge sheet against rider of the offending Motorcycle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC and 134(B) r/w Sec.187, 129, r/w 177, Sec.4 r/w Sec.181 of IMV Marimuthu vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68307231/

17 . The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioners have to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.
18.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 has taken contention that the respondent No.2 has violated the policy terms and conditions.
RW.1 in his chief-examination has stated that the insured has handed over the motorcycle to the minor at the time of accident and violated the policy conditions.
In the cross examination, the PW.1 has admitted that, the rider was minor.
On perusal of entire charge sheet, it appears that, the respondent No.1 has handed over the offending vehicle to the minor/juvenile and the offending vehicle was driven by the minor.

For the said reason, the charge sheet has been filed against the minor rider/juvenile for the offence punishable U/ Sec.279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC and 134(B) r/w Sec.187, 129, r/w 177, Sec.4 r/w Sec.181 of IMV Act.
Further filed the charge sheet against the respondent No.1 U/Sec.5(1) r/w Sec.181 of IMV Act.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that, respondent No.2 has violated the fundamental conditions of the policy.
Therefore, it clearly shows that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, this Court is of considered opinion that the respondent No.1 has proved that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

19. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1-F.I.R, Ex.P.2-complaint, Ex.P.3 the copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 the copy of seizure mahazar, Ex.P.5 the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.6 the copy of Inquest report, Ex.P.7 the copy of PM report, Ex.P.8 the charge sheet, Ex.P.9 the notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act and Ex.P.10 the reply to the notice, it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04/JH-1312.
Hence, this Tribunal is answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:
The petitioners claimed the compensation amount of Rs.40,00,000/- with respect to death of Sri.Hari Prasath in a road traffic accident.
21. As per Ex.P.11 Notarized Copy of Aadhaar Card
, date of year of the deceased is shown as 15-11-2003.
As per Ex.P.6 and 7 Inquest Report and PM report, the age of the deceased is shown as 19 years.
Accordingly relying on aadhar card, age of the deceased is considered about 19 years as on the date of accident.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the age of the deceased is 19 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier is 18.
22.

The petitioners have contended that, at the time of accident, the deceased was working as an employee at Private Company and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/-p.m. and contributing his entire earnings to maintain the family.

In support of the same, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.14 and P.15 the certificates of merit issued by RP-Sanjiv Group, the Economist, First Source, which shows that the deceased have completed training in the said Group of company, but they have neither examined the said employer before the Court and nor produced the pay slips or attendance register before the Court to prove the actual income and avocation of the deceased.
Therefore, by Marimuthu vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 July, 2025

considering the age, income and occupation of the deceased this Tribunal has taken the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
23.

With regard to the loss of future prospectus is concern, the Apex Court in the earlier Judgment reported in 2013 ACJ 1403 (Rajesh & Ors Vs Rajbir Singh & Ors) also taken note of the fact that, self employed persons are also entitled for future prospectus and the said Judgment was referred to larger bench and the Apex court in the recent Judgment passed in 2017 ACJ 2700 SC, between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and Others.

sentences.text: "In case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.

An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component"

Herein this case, the deceased was aged about 19 years, hence the petitioners are entitled to claim 40% of future prospectus as per above citation, due to death of the deceased in the road traffic accident.
24. The petitioner No.1 is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased.
Hence the petitioner No.1 and 2 being parents of the deceased are considered as dependents on the income of deceased.

So, relying upon the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Varma and others - Vs- Delhi Transport Corporation & another), out of the salary of the deceased 50% has to be deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased (as the deceased is a Bachelor/unmarried).

entities.text: 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Varma and others - Vs- Delhi Transport Corporation & another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Income of the deceased is taken at Rs. 16,000/- Addition of 40% income towards future prospectus:
 Rs. 22,400/-
Rs.16,000/- + 6,400/- (40%) =
22,400/-
Deduction towards personal expenses: Rs. 11,200/-
Rs.22,400/- - Rs.11,200/- (50%)
Therefore this tribunal took the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.11,200/-, which comes as Rs.11,200/- X 12 X 18 = Rs.24,19,200/-.
Hence, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.24,19,200/- under the head loss of dependency.
25. The petitioner No.1 & 2 are the parents of the deceased, they lost love, affection and future support of the deceased.
In this regard the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India was held in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & Ors., reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130.

sentences.text: The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation aimed at providing relief to the victims or their families, in cases of genuine claims.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Parental consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the Act.
A few High courts have awarded compensation on this count.
However, there was no clarity with respect to the principles on which compensation could be awarded on loss of Filial Consortium.
The amount of compensation to be awarded as consortium will be governed by the Principles of awarding compensation under "Loss of consortium" as laid down in Pranay Sethi (Supra).
In the present case, we deem it appropriate to award the father and the sister of the deceased, an amount of Rs.40,000/- each, for loss of Filial Consortium.
Hence, the petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation amount at Rs.40,000/- each under the head loss of Filial Consortium.

In total the petitioners are entitled for amount of Rs.80,000/-
under this head.

26. Further, the petitioners claimed compensation towards transportation of dead body, funeral &
obsequies ceremonies, but they had not produced any document.

However by considering the expenses towards funeral & obsequies ceremonies of deceased and in view of judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court passed in 2017 ACJ 2700 SC (between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others) it is just and proper to award a Rs.15,000/- under this head.

sentences.text: Further the petitioners are also entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head loss of estate.

27. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
 Under the Heads of: Amount 1. Loss of Dependency Rs. Rs.24,19,200/-
2. Towards Loss of Filial Rs. 80,000/-
 Consortium.
3. Towards Funeral and Obsequies Rs. 15,000/-
 Ceremonies 4.

Towards Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/-
 Total Rs. 25,29,200/-
The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,29,200/-.

For awarding interest, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest can be awarded in MVC Cases, cannot be more than 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Hence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.

29. Liability:-
The Respondent No.1 is the Insurer & Respondent No.2 is the RC Owner of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04/JH- 1312.

As already discussed in the issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle Reg.No.KA-04/JH-1312.
30.

The Counsel for the Respondent No.1 took specific contention that the rider of the offending vehicle was a minor and does not possessed the valid D.L. to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

The officer of the respondent No.1 is examined as RW.1 deposed that, the rider of the offending vehicle was minor and does not possessed the valid D.L. to ride the said vehicle as on the date of accident.
The K.R. Puram Traffic Police have filed the charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle as a juvenile.

Therefore,
it is clear that, as on the date of the accident, the offending vehicle was ridden by the minor and he was not having valid D.L.
31.
The respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the said motorcycle was ridden by the minor and he caused this accident.
Hence it is clear that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it is clear that the respondent No.2 knowing well that the rider of the motorcycle was minor permitted to ride the vehicle.
Hence it is also clear that the respondent No.2 has violated the policy conditions.

32. In this case the respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and she is knowing well that the rider was the minor and he is not having driving license and permitted the rider to ride her motorcycle and the minor caused this accident, hence the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners, but the respondent No.2 who is the owner of the offending motorcycle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
As such, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation.

Hence, issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
33.

Issue No.3: for the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

opennyai_summary.issue:
9. Based on the above pleadings, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that on 26-06- 2023 at about 3.30 pm, deceased Hari Prasath was proceeding as a pillion rider in a Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04/JH-1312 on Jayanthi Nagara Main Road, near D Mart Shop, Bangalore,
wherein the rider of the said motorcycle drove it, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering human life, without following any traffic rules and dashed against the Bicycle and caused the accident, due to forced impact deceased succumbed to the accidental injuries in the hospital?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so how much?
From whom?
3) Whether order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
17 . The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioners have to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

Therefore, it clearly shows that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, this Court is of considered opinion that the respondent No.1 has proved that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Herein this case, the deceased was aged about 19 years, hence the petitioners are entitled to claim 40% of future prospectus as per above citation, due to death of the deceased in the road traffic accident.
Hence the petitioner No.1 and 2 being parents of the deceased are considered as dependents on the income of deceased.
In this regard the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India was held in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & Ors., reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130.

The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation aimed at providing relief to the victims or their families, in cases of genuine claims.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Parental consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the Act.
The amount of compensation to be awarded as consortium will be governed by the Principles of awarding compensation under "Loss of consortium" as laid down in Pranay Sethi (Supra).
The respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the said motorcycle was ridden by the minor and he caused this accident.
Hence it is clear that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence it is also clear that the respondent No.2 has violated the policy conditions.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In the present case, we deem it appropriate to award the father and the sister of the deceased, an amount of Rs.40,000/- each, for loss of Filial Consortium.
Hence, the petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation amount at Rs.40,000/- each under the head loss of Filial Consortium.
In total the petitioners are entitled for amount of Rs.80,000/-
under this head.

 Total Rs. 25,29,200/-
The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,29,200/-.

ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
